questions.question: How many controls are there globally that influence the climate of a particular zone?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**6**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Six major controls influence the climate of a particular zone globally:
 
 
• **Latitude:** The latitude of a location determines the angle at which sunlight strikes the Earth's surface. Locations closer to the equator receive more direct sunlight and have warmer temperatures, while locations farther from the equator receive less direct sunlight and have cooler temperatures.
 
• **Altitude**: Altitude refers to the elevation of a location above sea level. As altitude increases, the atmosphere becomes thinner, and air pressure decreases. This reduced air pressure leads to cooler temperatures.
 
• **Distance from the sea:** Land heats up and cools down more quickly than water. Coastal areas tend to have more moderate temperatures than inland areas because the ocean moderates the temperature fluctuations.
 
• **Ocean currents:** Ocean currents transport heat around the globe. Warm ocean currents can bring warmer temperatures to coastal areas, while cold ocean currents can bring cooler temperatures.
 
• **Topography:** Topography refers to the physical features of a landscape, such as mountains and valleys. Mountains can block wind and precipitation patterns, while valleys can trap heat and moisture.
 
• **Prevailing winds:** Prevailing winds are the dominant wind patterns in a region. They can bring warm or cold air masses to an area, influencing the local climate.

CP on loss = SP × 100/(100 - Loss)

**Calculations:**

⇒ 300 - 288.27 = 11.73

% profit = 11.73/(185.18 + 103.09) × 100

questions.question: The largest number of four digits that is exactly divisible by 17 and 36 is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Identify the **LCM** of 17 and 36 first.

**LCM** (17, 36) = 17 × 36 = 612 (since 17 is a **prime number**).

Divide the largest 4-digit number (9999) by 612 to find the remainder.

9999 ÷ 612 → Remainder = 207.

**Largest number** = 9999 − 207 = 9792.

**∴ The correct answer is 9792.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Step 1:** Calculate **LCM** of 17 and 36.

⇒ 17 is prime, 36 = 2² × 3².

⇒ **LCM** = 17 × 36 = 612.

**Step 2:** Find the largest 4-digit multiple of 612.

⇒ Largest 4-digit number = 9999.

⇒ 9999 ÷ 612 = 16.33...

⇒ Required number = 612 × 16.

⇒ 612 × 16 = 9792.

**∴ The correct answer is 9792.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

If one number is **prime** and doesn't divide the other, their **LCM** is simply their product.

Divisibility Rule of 36

A number is divisible by 36 if it is divisible by both 4 (last two digits) and 9 (sum of digits).

To find the largest multiple of **n** below **L**, calculate **L − (L mod n)**.</p

questions.question: If a truck moves at a constant speed of 30 km/h for 1 kilometre and 45 km/h for the next 1 kilometre. What is the average speed of the truck?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

When a **truck** covers two equal distances at different speeds, the **Average Speed** is the **Harmonic Mean** of the two speeds.

Formula: Average Speed = (2 × v₁ × v₂) ÷ (v₁ + v₂)

Calculation: (2 × 30 × 45) ÷ (30 + 45) = 2700 ÷ 75 = 36 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 36 km/h.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

First speed (v₁) = 30 km/h, Distance (d₁) = 1 km

Second speed (v₂) = 45 km/h, Distance (d₂) = 1 km

**Formula Used:**

**Average Speed** = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/bf2cc828a1611862b2c39fa5b5a51d51ba8203d77e90643be407833937ecf4fc.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Distance = 1 km + 1 km = 2 km

⇒ Time taken for the first km (t₁) = Distance ÷ Speed = 1/30 hours

⇒ Time taken for the second km (t₂) = Distance ÷ Speed = 1/45 hours

⇒ Total Time = t₁ + t₂ = 1/30 + 1/45

⇒ Total Time = (3 + 2) ÷ 90 = 5/90 = 1/18 hours

⇒ Average Speed = 2 ÷ (1/18) = 2 × 18

⇒ Average Speed = 36 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 36 km/h.**

**__Additional Information__**

General Average Speed

Average speed is always calculated as the **Total Distance** divided by the **Total Time** taken for the entire journey.

Average Speed for Equal Time Intervals

If a body travels for two equal time intervals at speeds x and y, the average speed is the **Arithmetic Mean**: (x + y) ÷ 2.

Unit Conversion

To convert **km/h** to **m/s**, multiply the speed by 5/18. To convert **m/s** to **km/h**, multiply by 18/5.</p
